item.description: arXiv:2607.26561v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The recent gravitational-wave detection GW250114 by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) Collaboration provides unprecedented precision for testing general relativity (GR) through black hole ringdowns. In this study, we provide the first bounds on theory-agnostic deviations from the Teukolsky equation as described by the beyond-Teukolsky formalism. It directly connects deviations in the perturbation equations on the level of the effective potential in the Teukolsky equation with changes in the quasinormal mode (QNM) spectrum. We incorporate information on the final mass and spin from a full LVK inspiral-merger-ringdown analysis as parametrized priors in our analysis, reflecting theoretical uncertainties. Using publicly available LVK posterior information on agnostic damped sinusoid parameters, we then demonstrate how much beyond-Teukolsky potentials can be constrained. The high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) allows us to avoid the expensive full Bayesian analysis of all parameters and to work directly with a simplified likelihood for the fundamental QNM only. This strategy is promising for future events with even higher SNR and allows, in principle, for a quick and simple test of theories beyond GR without performing the full data analysis procedure. We report that current bounds on deviation parameters are in agreement with the Teukolsky equation.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian H. V\"olkel, Nicola Franchini

item.title: Kerr-NUT Thermodynamics: Misner Strings and Nut Charges
item.description: arXiv:2608.01152v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Using the thermodynamic approach introduced in e-Print: 2206.09124 [hep-th] to the case of Kerr-NUT solution, we demonstrate the existence of a new conserved quantity that is dual to the angular momentum, in the same way that the nut charge "n" is dual to the mass "m". This quantity exists regardless of the presence of the Kerr rotation parameter $a$, but only affects its thermodynamics when $a\neq 0$. The thermodynamic quantities calculated together with the two charges $N_{c}=cn$ and $N_{n}=n$ lead to consistent thermodynamic relations. That is, the first law, Smarr's and Gibbs-Duhem relations are all satisfied.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Tharwat, Adel Awad

item.title: Stability of perturbations around black holes under spatially extended potential deformations
item.description: arXiv:2608.06798v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: It has been shown that the spectrum of black hole quasi-normal modes is extremely sensitive to localized deformations of the geometry away from the potential peak. Deformations associated with a real astronomical environment may extend over a broad spatial region rather than be localized in a finite region. Whether spatially extended fluctuations distributed throughout spacetime can produce similar effects remains unclear. In this work, we construct a toy model to investigate spatially extended effective-potential deformations motivated by geometric or environmental fluctuations. We study how such deformations affect the corresponding perturbation system in the time domain. Using both the P\"oschl-Teller and scalar Regge-Wheeler potentials as representative backgrounds, we show that sufficiently wide oscillatory perturbations of zero mean can drive the corresponding perturbation systems from decay to exponential growth in the time domain. Through numerical analysis, we uncover a scaling relation for the instability threshold and further provide an analytical interpretation of its physical origin.
item.dc:creator: Shi-Jie Ma, Run-Qiu Yang

item.title: Two-Fluid Schwarzschild Solution
item.description: arXiv:2608.10552v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: \We consider the interior two-fluid Schwarzschild solution. That is a model of compact (neutron) stars with admixed dark matter. The two constant energy densities generalize the interior Schwarschild solution to the case of two fluids (representing standard model matter and dark matter, for instance), interacting mutually solely by the common gravitational field. In general, the two-fluid core is surrounded by a one-fluid corona (envelope). Only for special parameters (the model depends on energy densities $e_1,e_2$ and central pressures $p_{\mathrm{c}1},p_{\mathrm{c}2}$ of the fluids), both fluids occupy the same region. Despite the sum of two energy densities in that region, the compactness bound of 4/9 is not exceeded. Therefore, a Buchdahl limit for two fluids holds. A conceivable object is one with a stark leakage of one fluid (e.g. dark matter) beyond the two-fluid core.
item.dc:creator: Rico Z\"ollner, Burkhard K\"ampfer

item.title: How much averaged null energy must an anisotropic bounce violate?
item.description: arXiv:2608.29556v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that in Einstein gravity a null-complete, non-static Bianchi I universe (homogeneous, spatially flat and anisotropic) violates the averaged null energy condition (ANEC) along every complete light ray outside at most four null directions, and along all of them if its total energy density, cosmological constant included, is ever positive. Along each complete ray the averaged null energy is at most $-J_p/(8\pi G)$, with equality whenever the integral converges, where $J_p$ is the squared expansion and shear accumulated by a thin bundle of light rays. With spatial sections $\mathbb{R}^3$ the achronal ANEC therefore leaves only Minkowski space, as for flat and open Friedmann models. Under the pointwise null energy condition, every null geodesic of a non-static Bianchi I universe is incomplete. The isotropic bounce of effective loop quantum cosmology has $J_p=1.478\,\omega_B H_{\max}$ (light frequency at the bounce times largest Hubble rate), and at the same critical density the cheapest ray of a strongly anisotropic bounce pays four to five times as much. A Casimir-supported turning point on a three-torus has a deficit of the same order, but at Hubble rates well below the Planck scale its light rays circumnavigate the torus and are not achronal, so the achronal ANEC does not apply to them.
item.dc:creator: Alan Zhang, Ye Zhou

item.title: Universal Structure of Horizon Formation in Generic Binary Black Hole Mergers
item.description: arXiv:2609.11819v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A new common apparent horizon forms during a binary black hole merger and gives rise to outer and inner branches of marginally outer trapped surfaces. We derive the local structure of these branches. This event occurs in the fully nonlinear regime, outside the standard regimes of post-Newtonian inspiral theory and perturbations of a stationary black hole, yet it admits a universal description. Without assuming symmetry, we show that the stability operator of the marginally outer trapped surface must lose invertibility at formation. Outermost stability then implies that the vanishing eigenvalue is the principal one, with a strictly positive eigenfunction. Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction yields square-root branch separation with a shared linear drift. The outer and inner common horizons lie on a smooth marginally outer trapped tube along which slice time has a local minimum at formation, and nearby later slices intersect it in outer and inner branches whose separation scales as $(t-t_*)^{1/2}$. Sufficiently smooth quasilocal scalar functionals with nonzero first variation along the principal zero mode inherit the square-root separation and a shared linear term. We test these predictions in three binary black hole simulations, including an eccentric, precessing, unequal-mass system. In all three, the worldtube geometry and quasilocal scalars follow the predicted scaling. With the next-order term included, free-exponent fits to the surface geometry and quasilocal functionals recover the square-root exponent, $1/2$, to within half a percent, and diagnostics agree on the formation time within $5\times10^{-5}M$. The correlation between horizon shear and gravitational-wave news raises the possibility that common horizon formation has a signature in a short segment of the merger waveform.
item.dc:creator: Yu-Cun Xie, Vaishak Prasad

item.title: Revisiting the Frolov--Zelnikov solution for Majumdar--Papapetrou black holes
item.description: arXiv:2609.23921v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We revisit Frolov and Zelnikov's electrostatic Green function for a test charge in a multi-center Majumdar--Papapetrou spacetime, correcting its horizon-charge condition and extending the result to higher dimensions. In four dimensions, we derive the exact Dirichlet-to-Neumann map for a minimally coupled spectator Maxwell field with independently prescribed horizon potentials. The horizon flux charges obey a capacitance matrix with entries $C_{AA}=M_A+\sum_{B\ne A}M_AM_B/R_{AB}$ and $C_{AB}=-M_AM_B/R_{AB}$, where $M_A$ are center masses and $R_{AB}$ their separations. This matrix is a positive diagonal term plus a weighted graph Laplacian, yielding an exact common-mode/differential-mode decomposition of the field energy. The grounded Dirichlet Green function partitions a point charge's flux among infinity and the horizons through harmonic measures. We show that the diagonal condition imposed by Frolov and Zelnikov [Eq.~(4.14)] preserves only the total horizon charge, allowing redistribution between individual horizons. A corrected symmetric Green function preserving each horizon charge instead involves the inverse capacitance matrix. For two centers, the correction produces a finite, negative-semidefinite self-energy shift and an exact self-force difference, without additional ultraviolet subtraction. Finally, we extend the capacitance matrix, flux partition, and fixed-charge Green function to $D=n+3$ dimensions, where the graph weights contain the universal factor $\pi^{n/2}/\Gamma(n/2)$.
item.dc:creator: Jongheon Baek, Gihwan Nam

item.title: Black objects in a five-dimensional swirling spacetime
item.description: arXiv:2609.37511v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We use the Ehlers symmetry of the five-dimensional Ernst equation to embed the Myers-Perry black hole and the rotating black ring in a five-dimensional swirling spacetime. We show that both solutions can be made free of conical singularities, and that the swirl modifies the balance condition of the black ring. We compute horizon areas, surface gravities and Komar charges, which satisfy a Smarr relation, and study the ergoregions.
item.dc:creator: Adriano Vigan\`o

item.title: Scalar fields in the background of a linear Vaidya spacetime
item.description: arXiv:2610.24909v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study, in a semiclassical, quasi-stationary approximation, the entanglement properties of massless scalar fields near the event horizon of a dynamical black hole modeled by an ingoing Vaidya metric with a linearly decaying mass. In the near-horizon limit, the geometry becomes conformally equivalent to an eternal black hole, allowing the use of modular theory to analyze vacuum entanglement. We first study the modifications to the entanglement across the bifurcation surface of such a black hole from that of an eternal one. The conformal factor accounting for the evaporation modifies the Bogoliubov transformation between global modes and modes across the bifurcate Killing horizon of the black hole, inducing a phase in the thermofield-double-like structure of the global vacuum. This phase change of the vacuum state is a consequence of the adiabatic shift of the horizon. A quantitative measure of the entanglement change due to the phase is obtained through the Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) inequality. We compare the CHSH inequalities in the vacuum states for the static and the linear Vaidya black holes and find that the CHSH correlation quantity for the latter is decreased by a factor dependent on the evaporation rate. Next, we discuss the analysis of the linear Vaidya black hole formed from gravitational collapse. For this purpose we adapt an analysis by Wald for the case of the Schwarzschild black hole. The entangled global vacuum again has a thermofield double structure. However, we find, as expected, the near-horizon structure and state do not approach that of the eternal black hole. Rather, the thermal factor is modified by a factor incorporating the change in the black hole mass due to evaporation.
item.dc:creator: Arielle Schutz, Ratindranath Akhoury

item.title: Gravitational baryogenesis in Gauss-Bonnet braneworld cosmology
item.description: arXiv:2610.38188v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The present study investigates the feasibility of gravitational baryogenesis in a Gauss-Bonnet (GB) modified Randall-Sundrum (RS) type II braneworld cosmology. The modified expansion rate of the Universe in this scenario evolves through three distinct expansion regimes, the GB regime at early times where the expansion rate $H \sim \rho^{1/3}$ falls more slowly than the standard expansion law $H\sim \rho^{1/2}$ of GR, then the RS type era with an enhanced expansion $H \sim \rho$, before finally reducing to the standard expansion law in the low energy limit. Gravitational baryogenesis depends on $\dot{R}$ and requires $\dot{R} <0$. This condition is satisfied for the GB and GR regimes. However, $\dot{R}>0$ for the RS regime and successful baryogenesis requires either that the decoupling temperature occurs during the GB regime or that the Universe makes a direct transition from the GB regime to the GR regime. The GB baryon asymmetry $\eta(T)$ is proportional to $\mu (1+w)(1-w)(1+1/\beta)$, where $\mu$ is the energy scale $\mu \equiv 1/l$ associated with the bulk curvature scale $l$, $\beta \equiv 4 \alpha \mu^{2}$, where $\alpha$ is the GB coupling, and $w$ is the equation of state parameter $p=w \rho$. Studies of inflation in GB-braneworld cosmology place constraints on the allowed ranges of the parameters $\mu$ and $\beta$. Guided by these, the asymmetry has been calculated for ranges of $(\mu, \beta, w)$ and it is found that the observed values can be obtained for a value of $\beta$ within the range $(10^{-2} - 10^{-3})$ for $\mu =10^{12}$ GeV, and within the range $(10^{-1}- 10^{-2})$ for $\mu =10^{13}$ GeV. All values of $\eta$ for $\mu=10^{14}$ are too high. The parameter ranges for the decoupling temperatures required to produce the observed asymmetry have also been established.
item.dc:creator: Ian B Whittingham

item.title: Light Ring Stability Across Spacetime Dimensions and Theories of Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2611.01917v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The light ring theorem states that four-dimensional stationary, axisymmetric, horizonless ultracompact objects (UCOs) possess light rings (LRs) in pairs, one of which is stable if the Null Energy Condition (NEC) holds in General Relativity (GR). The existence of a stable LR may trigger nonlinear spacetime instabilities, thereby raising questions about the viability of UCOs as long-lived black hole mimickers. We extend the LR existence and stability theorem beyond four-dimensional GR to modified gravity theories, in particular, $f(R)$ gravity, scalar-tensor theories, restricted Horndeski gravity and Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet (EGB) gravity, in ($d \geq 4$) dimensional spacetimes. Our findings show that in four-dimensional modified gravities, the stability of LRs is governed by theory-specific coupling parameters in addition to the NEC. Consequently, a stable LR is not guaranteed to occur in certain parameter regimes. In higher dimensions ($d>4$), we confirm using topological arguments that LRs still emerge in pairs; however, the topological charges are now associated with four distinct types of LRs, including two types of saddle points. The stability analysis further constrains the allowed LR pairings, implying that, unlike in four-dimensional GR, the emergent pair does not necessarily include a stable LR. Our findings directly impact tests of GR using UCOs, demonstrating that LR stability is highly sensitive to both the underlying gravitational theory and spacetime dimensionality.
item.dc:creator: Kajol Paithankar, Sanved Kolekar

item.title: Particle dynamics in rotating charged Bumblebee black holes: An analytical correspondence with Kerr-Newman
item.description: arXiv:2611.04750v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we establish an analytical correspondence between the equatorial dynamics of spinless and spinning test particles in a slowly rotating charged Einstein--Bumblebee black hole spacetime and those in an effective Kerr--Newman spacetime. For spinning particles, the correspondence is established within the Mathisson--Papapetrou--Dixon framework under appropriate parameter matching. We show that corresponding circular orbits have identical radii and coordinate angular velocities, while their radial dynamics and local instability rates exhibit a Lorentz-violation-dependent scaling. Nevertheless, the correspondence does not imply complete dynamical equivalence, as orbital trajectories and radial perturbation growth over an azimuthal period generally differ. These results delineate the scope and limitations of the effective Kerr--Newman correspondence by distinguishing the dynamical properties preserved under parameter matching from those modified by the Lorentz-violating radial deformation.
item.dc:creator: Xiaowei Li, Deyou Chen, Chuang Yang

item.title: Probing Lorentz-violating electrodynamics with CMB polarization
item.description: arXiv:2212.04867v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We perform a comprehensive study of the signatures of Lorentz violation in electrodynamics on the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) anisotropies. In the framework of the minimal Standard Model Extension (SME), we consider effects generated by renormalizable operators, both CPT-odd and CPT-even. These operators are responsible for sourcing, respectively, cosmic birefringence and circular polarization. We propagate jointly the effects of all the relevant Lorentz-violating parameters to CMB observables and provide constraints with the most recent CMB datasets. We bound the CPT-even coefficient to $k_{F,E+B} < 6.02 \times 10^{-32}$ at 95\% CL. This improves previous CMB bounds by more than one order of magnitude. The limits we obtain on the CPT-odd coefficients, i.e. $|k_{(V)00}^{(3)}| < 1.05 \times 10^{-44} \; {\rm GeV}$ and $|\mathbf{k_{AF}}| < 0.51 \times 10^{-44} \; {\rm GeV}$ at 95\% CL, are respectively one and two orders of magnitude stronger than previous CMB-based limits, superseding also bounds from non-CMB searches. This analysis provides the strongest constraints to date on CPT-violating coefficients in the minimal SME from CMB searches.
item.dc:creator: Luca Caloni, Serena Giardiello, Margherita Lembo, Martina Gerbino, Giulia Gubitosi, Massimiliano Lattanzi, Luca Pagano

item.title: Random matrix product state models of gravitationally prepared states
item.description: arXiv:2512.11966v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Gravitationally prepared states are quantum field theoretic states prepared by gravitational path integrals with spatial boundaries that have fixed boundary conditions for gravity but not for matter fields. They can be interpreted as quantum field theoretic states of closed universes encoding quantum gravitational effects of the past. We propose a method of modeling gravitationally prepared states in two dimensions with random matrix product states (RMPS). Such RMPS models allow us to compute quantities which include contributions of higher topologies and replica geometries to all orders. The bra-ket wormhole phase transition is a crucial physical property of gravitationally prepared states. We show that a RMPS model shows behavior qualitatively similar to the bra-ket wormhole phase transition if it satisfies the spectral gapping property, which we define. We define a class of models called $\mathrm{O}(k)$ models satisfying this property. A novel advantage of RMPS models is that they allow us to compute effects corresponding to off-shell wormholes, i.e., wormhole topologies without semiclassical solutions. In particular, numerical results in RMPS models suggest that off-shell wormholes lead to nonzero long-distance correlators in gravitationally prepared states. We also define RMPS models in continuous space, and discuss implications for studying de Sitter gravitationally prepared states.
item.dc:creator: Sunghoon Jung, Sungjung Kim, Jiwoo Park, Seokhyeon Song

item.title: Crossing symmetry of OPE statistics
item.description: arXiv:2512.21258v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the crossing symmetry of the ensemble of large-$c$ 2D CFTs defined through 3D gravity. A central observation is that statistical moments of OPE coefficients are not independent; rather, lower and higher moments are strongly correlated. Using Virasoro TQFT, we clarify how these correlations arise and how they guarantee consistency across OPE channels. Our analysis introduces the new notion of pseudo-hyperbolic manifolds, which are a certain class of non-hyperbolic manifolds whose partition functions are nevertheless related to those of hyperbolic ones. These manifolds serve as bridges that help manifest the crossing symmetry of the CFT ensemble.
item.dc:creator: Diandian Wang

item.title: Decoupling of large-scale, adiabatic inflationary perturbations from enhanced small-scale modes at one-loop
item.description: arXiv:2601.14229v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We reconsider back-reaction from large amplitude, short-scale perturbations onto a long wavelength adiabatic mode. In a loop expansion of the long-mode power spectrum, this back-reaction appears first at 1-loop. Due to the separation between the long and short scales, the separate universe method provides a simple and efficient framework for this computation. In this paper, building on our earlier work, we employ a $\delta N$ formula for the long mode, which captures the effect of short scales. We show that back-reaction at 1-loop is due to either (i) non-linearity of the $\delta N$ formula, or (ii) 1-loop corrections to the initial conditions. We argue that contributions of type (ii) cannot themselves be described within the separate universe framework, but their properties can be constrained using soft theorems and a ''multi-point propagator'' expansion. When applied to a band of enhanced short-scale perturbations that crossed the horizon during inflation, our result shows that the loop correction decouples from their detailed properties. Furthermore, the back-reaction we obtain is scale-invariant. Its magnitude is model-dependent, but is degenerate with effects from modes that were still sub-horizon at the end of inflation. In this scenario (but not necessarily in all scenarios), we conclude that the effect is not observable.
item.dc:creator: Laura Iacconi, David Mulryne, David Seery

item.title: Amplifying the Cosmological Collider with Ghost Spectators
item.description: arXiv:2601.14413v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Ghost inflation is a well-known framework in which cosmological fluctuations can generate enhanced primordial non-Gaussianity, typically of the equilateral type. In its original form, however, it is in tension with current observational constraints. Here we instead consider a setup in which a standard inflaton drives the background evolution, while excitations of a ghost condensate act as spectator fields that interact with the inflaton. This proposal fits naturally within the cosmological collider program: the exchanged particle has a modified dispersion relation, $\omega \propto k^2$. We show that this ghost-inspired dynamics weakens the usual Boltzmann suppression, similarly to models with a very small effective sound speed, yielding an enhanced bispectrum signal relative to standard cosmological collider scenarios. At the same time, the horizon-crossing scale remains a free parameter of the theory. As a result, the model shares features of both the de Sitter bootstrap and boostless frameworks. Finally, we derive the differential equations governing cosmological correlators in the ghost-collider setup. Their structure reflects the quadratic momentum dependence of the dispersion relation and distinguishes this scenario from conventional relativistic cases.
item.dc:creator: Matheus C. Ferreira, Felipe T. Falciano, Guilherme L. Pimentel

item.title: A Generalized Landauer's Principle for Unitarily Transformed Thermal Reservoirs
item.description: arXiv:2602.04552v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Landauer's principle, a cornerstone of quantum information and thermodynamics, appears to be violated when the thermal reservoir is replaced by a squeezed thermal state (STS), owing to the additional thermodynamic resources inherently present in the squeezed state. We introduce a formal extension of the principle to such unitarily transformed thermal states. By defining an effective Hamiltonian, we rigorously establish a generalized Landauer inequality, which naturally reduces to the standard case for an ordinary thermal reservoir as a special instance. The framework further yields a consistent definition of entropy production and a proof of its non-negativity. We illustrate its utility by studying an arbitrarily moving Unruh-DeWitt detector coupled to a quantum field initially prepared in the STS. Using perturbation theory, we compute the entropy production explicitly, confirming its positivity. As a result of the symmetry breaking induced by the unitary transformation, it depends on both the proper time interval and the absolute spacetime position. Our work clarifies the apparent violation of Landauer's principle with STSs by providing a consistent information-theoretic framework. It also offers a practical tool for computing entropy production in non-equilibrium and relativistic settings, with potential implications for quantum thermal machines and information protocols.
item.dc:creator: Hao Xu

item.title: A Holographic Model for Soft Photons and Gravitons in Four Dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2603.14499v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct a two-dimensional action on the celestial sphere that describes the infrared sector of Abelian gauge and gravitational theories in four dimensions. In particular, we use the holographic model to reproduce (1) antipodal matching conditions for the superphaserotation and supertranslation Goldstone modes in four dimensions, (2) leading soft photon and graviton theorems, and (3) infrared factorization of amplitudes with generic dressed $in$ and $out$ states. Using (3), we reproduce the infrared divergences that plague the standard undressed amplitudes, and show that amplitudes involving Faddeev-Kulish dressed states are infrared finite. As a corollary, we use our holographic model to construct an infinite class of dressed states that give rise to infrared finite scattering amplitudes.
item.dc:creator: Sangmin Choi, Prahar Mitra

item.title: Decoherence and the Reemergence of Coherence From a Superconducting "Horizon"
item.description: arXiv:2603.16765v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In a recent paper [arXiv:2205.06279], Danielson et al. demonstrated that the mere presence of a black hole causes universal decoherence of quantum superpositions (dubbed the DSW decoherence). We analyze decoherence in a superconducting analogue [arXiv:1709.06154] of the event horizon of a late-stage black hole, where Andreev reflection plays the role of Hawking radiation. We consider a normal metal interferometer threaded by an Aharonov-Bohm flux, where one of the arms of the interferometer is coupled to a superconductor by a tunnel coupling of varying strength. At absolute zero temperature and for weak coupling, we find that the scattering states of the interferometer are decohered by Andreev reflection, a nontrivial manifestation of the proximity effect analogous to DSW decoherence from the event horizon of a black hole. However, for increasing coupling strength to the superconductor, we find a reemergence of coherence via resonant tunneling through Andreev bound states. This suggests the existence of an analogue gravitational phenomenon wherein transmission mediated by virtual Hawking radiation leads to a reemergence of coherence in an interferometer placed near a black hole's event horizon.
item.dc:creator: Eric J. Sung, Charles A. Stafford

item.title: Observational Tests for Distinguishing Classes of Cosmological Models
item.description: arXiv:2604.07244v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate observational tests that can be used to distinguish between broad classes of cosmological models. This is achieved using curvature-consistency tests of the Friedmann-Lema\^{i}tre-Robertson-Walker (FLRW) models, which we investigate in two scenarios where they can be violated; (i) when the optical properties of the cosmology deviate from the expectations of FLRW, and also (ii) when the large-scale expansion of the cosmology is different from FLRW. We identify useful ways to determine the properties of these alternative scenarios in terms of the violation of the curvature-consistency tests, and propose a new null test that can be used to isolate cosmologies with non-FLRW observational relations. The characteristic signatures we find can be used, together with the results of recent and upcoming cosmological observations, to probe and/or rule out large classes of cosmological models. This becomes an increasingly important task as the number of proposals in the literature increases, as cosmologists attempt to explain tensions, anomalies, and the dark sector of the Universe. Our approach provides a clear route for telling apart these different proposals, and offers a new opportunity for using precision cosmological data to efficiently discriminate between cosmological models.
item.dc:creator: Asta Heinesen, Timothy Clifton

item.title: All-order structure of static gravitational interactions and the seventh post-Newtonian potential
item.description: arXiv:2604.14134v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a closed formula for the computation of static post-Newtonian corrections to the two-body gravitational dynamics at any odd order, assuming the lower-order results are known. The formula is derived within a correlation function framework and exploits the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry of the static sector, leading to a novel theoretical interpretation of the factorization theorem. As an application, we compute the gravitational interaction of two compact coalescing objects at the seventh post-Newtonian order in the static limit, which receives contributions from seven-loop graphs at order $\mathcal{O}(G_N^8 v^0)$, and find complete agreement with the results obtained using the diagrammatic approach of the factorization theorem.
item.dc:creator: Giacomo Brunello, Manoj K. Mandal, Pierpaolo Mastrolia, Raj Patil, Matteo Pegorin, Sid Smith, Jan Steinhoff

item.title: Caustic Skeleton and the Local Cosmic Web: the Coma Cluster node and the Pisces-Perseus ridge
item.description: arXiv:2604.22213v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We apply caustic skeleton theory to the Manticore-Local simulations, which are Bayesian constrained reconstructions of the Local Universe from the 2M++ galaxy catalogue, and extract the three-dimensional multi-scale caustic skeleton of two canonical weblike structures in our Local Universe, namely the Coma Cluster and the Pisces-Perseus ridge as they represent the most prominent cluster node and filamentary artery in the nearby Universe. We show that the Caustic Skeleton network of caustic singularities accurately reproduces the observed large-scale organisation of galaxies in redshift space for one of the Manticore realisations. The hierarchy of caustic features allows us to establish a multi-scale classification of the large-scale environment in which observed 2M++ galaxies reside. One of the most interesting aspects of the theory is that it predicts two topologically distinct classes of filaments (A_4 swallowtail and D_4 umbilic caustics) that form through fundamentally different folding histories. We find that the A_4 filaments form the most outstanding filamentary features of our local universe, whereas D_4 filaments appear to largely collect at cluster regions identified in the galaxy distribution. Thus, a preliminary galaxy classification scheme presented in this study finds indications of a higher proportion of galaxies in D_4/Node-dominated environments in the Pisces-Perseus Supercluster, which may be indicative of more clumpy substructure along its ridge, compared to the extended weblike structure around the Coma Cluster. [Shortened]
item.dc:creator: Amelie Read, Job Feldbrugge, Celine Boehm, Rien van de Weygaert, Benjamin Hertzsch

item.title: Carrollian quantum states and flat space holography
item.description: arXiv:2604.22745v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study free Carrollian quantum field theories from an algebraic perspective and explore their implications for flat space holography. As explicit examples, we construct the electric and magnetic Carrollian Weyl algebras obtained from Carroll limits of the relativistic scalar field and analyze their states, including vacuum and thermal configurations. For the massive electric theory, we find a regular Carroll-invariant vacuum state and a regular KMS state, yielding a consistent Carrollian thermodynamic system. By contrast, the massless electric and magnetic theories are more subtle: depending on the quantization, they admit either no regular distinguished vacuum or only nonregular Carroll-invariant ground states, while still supporting nonregular thermal states. We further analyze alternative classes of states in the massless electric theory, including spatially homogeneous quasifree pure states and Sorkin--Johnston states. Motivated by these results, we discuss consequences for flat space holography. We construct a well-defined state relevant for Carrollian holography whose Hilbert-space representation factorizes into a standard Fock sector and a nonseparable zero-mode sector, thereby highlighting the role of infrared degrees of freedom in the boundary theory.
item.dc:creator: Stefan Fredenhagen, Stefan Prohazka, Robert Tiefenbacher

item.title: Non-Gaussian Halo Bias from Tensor-Induced Density Perturbations
item.description: arXiv:2605.02882v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Primordial gravitational waves induce matter density perturbations at second order. Because this sourcing is quadratic in tensor modes, the induced density field is intrinsically non-Gaussian even for Gaussian tensor modes. Here we compute the scale-dependent halo-bias correction generated by this tensor-induced density bispectrum for a Gaussian-bump tensor spectrum with a peak tensor-to-scalar ratio $r_*=0.002$. At low wavenumbers, both the induced density power spectrum and the bispectrum form factor approach finite, nonzero constants. Their ratio consequently produces a large-scale plateau in the bias correction defined relative to the tensor-induced density power spectrum. Over the sampled scales, the fractional Eulerian correction reaches a maximum of $1.85\times10^{-10}$. When evaluated relative to the total matter power spectrum, the fractional correction remains below $4.0\times10^{-25}$ across the sampled scales and halo populations. Its scale dependence differs from that of the standard local, equilateral, and enfolded primordial non-Gaussianity templates.
item.dc:creator: Mariam Abdelaziz, Pritha Bari, Sabino Matarrese, Angelo Ricciardone

item.title: An algebra of proper observables at null infinity: Dirac brackets, Memory and Goldstone probes
item.description: arXiv:2605.13804v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a rigorous evaluation of Dirac brackets for classical observables on the phase space of radiative gravitational modes at null infinity that naturally incorporates memory effects. Considering the Ashtekar-Streubel phase space, with boundary conditions in time given by vanishing {\it news} and purely electric {\it shear}, and taking into account the infinite dimensionality of the phase space, we identify the algebra of proper observables (understood as functions on phase space that can be associated with smooth symplectic flows). We show that the action of supertranslation charges generate the correct transformations on the shear. We also show that the conventional definition of the ``Goldstone mode'' adopted in the literature cannot be associated with a proper observable, but nevertheless there exists an infinite family of proper observables, which we call {\it Goldstone probes}, that are capable of measuring the Goldstone mode. We notice that there are no Goldstone probes constructed only out of the shear {\it or} the news, providing a possible explanation for why attempts to construct a (separable) Hilbert space with different memory states have failed so far. Finally, we derive formulas for distributional Dirac brackets between local shear and news, and show that they contain non-local corrections.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Andrade e Silva, Simone Speziale

item.title: QPEs from Warped Disk Collisions with EMRIs: Brightness-Recurrence Diagram and Gravitational-Wave Follow-up
item.description: arXiv:2605.24905v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Quasi-Periodic Eruptions (QPEs) display correlated long/short and strong/weak patterns that remain unexplained by existing flat-disk collision models. We propose that these features arise from an extreme-mass-ratio inspiral (EMRI) colliding with a warped accretion disk, likely formed after a tidal disruption event. The warp modulates both recurrence time and burst energy, encoding the disk geometry -- and thus the spin of the central supermassive black hole (SMBH) -- into the X-ray light curve. We introduce the Brightness-Recurrence Diagram (BRD) to visualize this correlation, where QPE bursts trace an elliptical trajectory driven by the EMRI's apsidal precession; the tilt of this ellipse encodes whether the EMRI is prograde or retrograde relative to the SMBH spin. Applying this model to the prototypical QPE source GSN 069 successfully reproduces the observed patterns. The data are consistent with either a prograde stellar secondary or a retrograde stellar-mass black hole. In the stellar-mass black hole scenario, ongoing orbital decay could render the EMRI detectable by LISA within a few decades, facilitating gravitational-wave follow-up and independent multimessenger constraints on the system.
item.dc:creator: Bo-An Chen, Bei You, Giovanni Miniutti, Ning Jiang, Zhen Pan, Tao Yang, Xi-Long Fan, Kai Liao, Xu-Heng Ding, Zong-Hong Zhu, Shuai-Kang Yang, Sai-En Xu, Han He, Xiao Fan

item.title: Coherent Entanglement between Massive Oscillators from the Quantized Gravitational Field
item.description: arXiv:2606.12901v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work, we investigate how entanglement between two massive quantum particles trapped in harmonic oscillator potentials is generated after they interact with propagating modes of the quantized gravitational field. Specifically, we consider only the entanglement arising from the coherent contribution of the gravitational field to investigate its causal structure. We employ the Feynman-Vernon influence functional approach, within which the contribution of the coherent gravitational field to entanglement generation can be traced to the commutation relation of the gravitational field. Our analysis shows that entanglement does not arise instantaneously after the interaction begins. Instead, there is a time delay proportional to the separation between the two particles before entanglement begins to develop. This result shows that the entanglement arising from the coherent contribution of the gravitational field exhibits a causal structure. The magnitude of the resulting entanglement is generally very small. However, when the initial quantum states of the two particles are prepared as separable squeezed states, the resulting entanglement can be enhanced, with the magnitude of the enhancement depending exponentially on the squeezing parameter.
item.dc:creator: Anom Trenggana, Freddy P. Zen

item.title: Mapping Domain-Wall Bayesian Reconstruction with LISA
item.description: arXiv:2606.15387v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the Bayesian reconstruction of peaked domain-wall gravitational-wave signals with LISA and construct reconstruction maps over the signal-parameter plane. These maps identify regions where the signal can be probed with minimal posterior uncertainty and parameter degeneracy. Our analysis employs a two-parameter domain-wall spectral template and includes astrophysical foregrounds from Galactic double-white-dwarf binaries and extragalactic compact binaries, together with LISA instrumental noise. Bayesian inference is performed for 64 injections using nested sampling, and the resulting posterior quantities are interpolated with the Clough--Tocher method to generate smooth maps across parameter space. Under the adopted instrumental-noise and foreground assumptions, we find that LISA reconstructs domain-wall signals most effectively for annihilation temperatures $T_*\sim10^3\!-\!10^6\,\mathrm{GeV}$. In this regime, posteriors become tighter and less degenerate, enabling reliable two-parameter reconstruction. The most favorable region corresponds to signals with ${\rm SNR}\gtrsim50$, while signals with ${\rm SNR}\sim10$ remain reconstructable near $T_*\sim10^{5-6}\,\mathrm{GeV}$. This weaker-signal region corresponds approximately to $4\times10^{-12}\lesssim\Omega_{\rm GW}^{\rm peak}h^2\lesssim4\times10^{-11}$ and $30\,\mathrm{mHz}\lesssim f_p\lesssim100\,\mathrm{mHz}$. Our results provide a quantitative reconstruction forecast for peaked domain-wall signals in the LISA band and a guide for particle-physics models predicting milli-Hz gravitational-wave spectra.
item.dc:creator: Satyabrata Datta, Rome Samanta

item.title: Dressed Fock Spaces in Gauge Theory and Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2606.15988v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Four-dimensional gauge and gravitational theories exhibit long-range interactions that require asymptotic particles to be dressed by clouds of soft photons and gravitons. Faddeev-Kulish dressings render scattering amplitudes infrared-finite, but the resulting multi-particle states do not factorise into tensor products of dressed one-particle states. We show that this loss of Fock-space factorisation is not fundamental, but reflects an inappropriate choice of infrared variables. The real soft divergence is reproduced by the Goldstone modes of asymptotic symmetries, while the Coulomb phase is reproduced by new zero modes of the radiative fields that we introduce here. In these variables, infrared-finite dressed multi-particle states admit the usual Fock-space factorisation into single-particle dressed states.
item.dc:creator: Sangmin Choi, Prahar Mitra

item.title: Conformal boundary rigidity from null geodesic travel times
item.description: arXiv:2606.28689v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The gravitational field of a distant, isolated system is manifested by the conformally invariant Weyl tensor. Thus the conformal structure far from the system encodes the system's gravitational mass. It also encodes the causal structure, thereby linking it to the mass. For asymptotically anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetimes, this link led to a novel positive mass theorem of Page, Surya, and the second author \cite{PSW} which did not rely on any traditional energy condition. Here we ask whether that theorem has a rigidity case. Specifically, we consider all null geodesics in an asymptotically AdS spacetime that depart from the Penrose conformal infinity, travel through spacetime, and return to conformal infinity. If all such geodesics from a given point refocus at an antipodal point at infinity, is the spacetime conformal to anti-de Sitter space? It is easy to answer the question if the asymptotically AdS spacetime either (i) obeys the null energy condition in 3 or 4 spacetime dimensions, or (ii) is static (in any dimension), and we give simple proofs in those cases. We then answer the question in the case of globally stationary, asymptotically AdS spacetimes, by applying the theory of magnetic geodesics on the Riemannian manifold-with-boundary obtained by quotienting by the stationary Killing vector field. The question has an analogue for asymptotically flat spacetimes, which we also discuss.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Paternain, Eric Woolgar

item.title: Anisotropic separate universe : Long-wavelength perturbations and conserved quantities
item.description: arXiv:2607.11814v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the superhorizon evolution of linear perturbations in an anisotropic Bianchi type I universe with a scalar field coupled to a U(1) gauge field. The analysis employs the spatial gradient expansion in the uniform-$\mathcal{N}$ gauge, in which the local number of $e$-folds is unperturbed. In this gauge, the complete set of leading-order long-wavelength solutions, including both even- and odd-parity perturbations, can be constructed from variations of homogeneous Bianchi type I solutions, subject to the momentum and Gauss constraints. The conserved Wronskian found in isotropic multi-field inflation is generalized to the anisotropic system. Together with the shear and electric-flux integration constants, it allows the curvature perturbation on uniform-$\mathcal{N}$ hypersurfaces to be expressed in terms of background variations and time integrals. The conserved comoving curvature perturbations are then obtained by adding this intrinsic curvature contribution to the familiar $\delta N$ contribution arising from the change of time slicing. We also derive a relation between the curvature perturbation and a metric perturbation that reduces to the plus-polarized tensor mode in the isotropic limit, and discuss a nonlinear extension of the formalism.
item.dc:creator: Daiki Saito, Atsushi Naruko

item.title: Alternative Boundary Conditions in Asymptotically Anti-de Sitter Spacetimes
item.description: arXiv:2609.10805v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetimes are not globally hyperbolic, so boundary conditions are generally needed for well-defined dynamics. Ishibashi and Wald (IW) determined boundary conditions yielding well-posed dynamics with conserved positive energy for scalar, electromagnetic, and linearized gravitational fields, using nonlocal potentials and individual spherical harmonic modes. In this paper, we determine which IW conditions are local in the primary fields and which are AdS-invariant. In four spacetime dimensions, the standard AdS-invariant boundary conditions set the rescaled magnetic field to zero for electromagnetism and the rescaled magnetic Weyl tensor to zero for Einstein gravity on the conformal boundary. We generalize these standard boundary conditions by setting arbitrary linear combinations of the electric and magnetic fields, or the corresponding Weyl tensors, to zero, and we conjecture that these exhaust the local, AdS-invariant, conservative boundary conditions in AdS$_{1,3}$. Boundary conditions with non-AdS-invariance and in different spacetime dimensions are also studied. The AdS-invariant conditions in AdS$_{1,3}$ extend to Yang-Mills theory and nonlinear gravity in a general Fefferman-Graham setting. We construct phase spaces for these general boundary conditions. The covariant phase spaces for general conditions are naturally associated with Lagrangians containing Pontryagin terms and, in gravity, a Gauss-Bonnet term. In gravity, except for the standard boundary condition, no nontrivial asymptotic symmetries exist and all conserved charges such as ADM mass vanish identically, as in a closed universe. Spacetimes with Killing fields including AdS then exhibit linearization instability in the sense of Fischer and Marsden and Moncrief. For nonstandard boundary conditions, the modified symplectic structure yields new expressions for the entropy formula of black holes.
item.dc:creator: Robert M. Wald, Xinkang Wang

item.title: Nash Equilibrium from Quantum-Field Entanglement
item.description: arXiv:2609.33188v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Entanglement harvesting allows localized probes to extract entanglement from a quantum field, even when their interaction regions are spacelike separated. However, how the resource obtained by the probes can be operationalized remains largely open. In this work, we ask whether the harvested entanglement can influence the timing choices of observers acting as players. We construct a quantum input game for Alice and Bob, each controlling an Unruh-DeWitt detector that couples to the vacuum of a free massless scalar field in four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime. Each player can choose an early interaction time, a late interaction time, or exit. After joint entry, a referee sends independent question qubits, so that fixed local Bell measurements and a payment table convert the detector state into a payoff. The mean payoff is proportional to minus the expectation value of an entanglement witness and is nonpositive for every separable resource. We calculate the detector state to leading perturbative order and solve the participation game analytically. Away from payoff degeneracies, every timing equilibrium with positive payoff gives two trembling hand perfect participation equilibria, in addition to mutual exit. The total count can therefore be one, three, five, or seven. For one fixed switching function and timing menu, five selected delays give the sequence seven, three, one, seven, and one. The timing payoffs follow from the field's two-point functions, with the Hadamard and Pauli-Jordan contributions to the coherence competing against local excitation noise. The resulting equilibrium structure provides an operational setting for studying how vacuum correlations and causal propagation affect the strategic use of quantum-field entanglement.
item.dc:creator: Hao Xu

item.title: Almost-splitting of spacetimes under timelike sectional curvature bounds
item.description: arXiv:2610.10051v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish an almost-splitting theorem for spacetimes under timelike sectional curvature bounds in the spirit of the celebrated Riemannian result due to Cheeger and Colding. More concretely, we show that if a globally hyperbolic spacetime with timelike sectional curvature bounded below by a nonpositive constant close to zero contains a long maximizing timelike segment, then causal diamonds along that segment are close in the Lorentzian Gromov--Hausdorff sense of Minguzzi--Suhr to those in a product metric spacetime. Our result can be interpreted as a quantitative analogue of the Lorentzian splitting theorem for spacetimes with nonnegative timelike sectional curvature by Beem--Ehrlich--Markvorsen--Galloway. In contrast to the Riemannian setting, the timelike sectional curvature bound cannot be replaced by Ricci-flatness, as the small mass limit of the Schwarzschild exterior geometry shows.
item.dc:creator: Nicola Gigli, Melanie Graf, Robert J. McCann, Argam Ohanyan, Eric Woolgar, Matteo Zanardini

item.title: TheoPhysEval: Assessing AI agents at autonomous theoretical physics problem solving
item.description: arXiv:2610.16733v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a suite of 50 unpublished research-level theoretical physics problems with verifiable answers. Without AI assistance, a typical problem in our collection could be solved by a world expert in about a day or less but would take considerably longer for experts in adjacent specialties. We test the ability of off-the-shelf AI agents to tackle these problems autonomously, without human hints. When given access to tools available in a realistic setting, including the ability to search the literature and write scripts for numerical and symbolic work, the best-performing agent, GPT-6-Astra harnessed in Codex, obtains the final answers with a near-perfect accuracy of 98% at an average cost under USD 3 per problem. On average, agents show only small changes in accuracy when denied web search and access to background research papers, suggesting significant memorization of the literature. These results suggest that state-of-the-art agents can accurately perform concrete calculations required across theoretical physics research. We comment on the broader implications of these findings and discuss possible explanations for the current lack of agent-led breakthroughs in theoretical physics despite their outstanding problem-solving abilities.

item.title: Mechanical angular momentum loss at $\mathcal{O}(G^4)$ from static and radiative gravitons
item.description: arXiv:2610.26822v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We determine the loss of mechanical angular momentum $L^{\mu}_{\rm loss}$ of two gravitationally scattering bodies at $\mathcal{O}(G^4)$ using worldline quantum field theory (WQFT). The gravitational memory effect, a phenomenon of the early- and late-time behaviour of the gravitational field, leads to static contributions to $L^{\mu}_{\rm loss}$. We illuminate how these arise: the linear memory contributes through so-called static correlators, while the nonlinear memory vanishes at this order due to symmetry considerations. The computation of the remaining, dynamical part resembles that of the $\mathcal{O}(G^4)$ impulse. We generate its integrand using a reformulation of the WQFT Feynman rules that conserves four-momentum at every vertex and plainly exhibits the classical loops. The three-loop integrals are reduced to master integrals, whose differential equations and boundary matching in the post-Newtonian limit we describe in some detail. In contrast to conservative effects at this order, only polylogarithms appear. While individual contributions to the dynamical part are divergent, these cancel in $L^{\mu}_{\rm loss}$. The quadratic-in-radiation part of our result reproduces earlier results, while the complete result agrees with existing post-Newtonian results.
item.dc:creator: Lara Bohnenblust, Carl Jordan Eriksen, Gustav Uhre Jakobsen, Kathrin Stoldt, Andrii Yanovets

item.title: DBI Softens Stiff-Phase Gravitational-Wave Spectra
item.description: arXiv:2611.03429v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the effect of non-canonical kinetic terms on the present-day density spectrum of primordial gravitational waves (GWs), by considering the dynamics of a scalar field governed by the Dirac--Born--Infeld (DBI) action and a runaway potential. The field, responsible for a period of inflation, subsequently enters a kinetically dominated regime, where the DBI structure reduces the equation-of-state parameter relative to the canonical kination result $w=1$, thereby softening the blue tilt of the GW spectrum. Simultaneously, the energy density of the field redshifts at a slower rate, delaying radiation domination and prolonging the stiff phase. The interplay between these two effects can lead to a potentially observable GW signal that would otherwise remain beyond the reach of future experiments in the canonical case. We test our predictions by numerically solving the background and perturbations, from inflation until radiation domination, and find viable parameter space compatible with cosmic microwave background and Big Bang Nucleosynthesis constraints.
item.dc:creator: Samuel S\'anchez L\'opez, Eemeli Tomberg, Juan C. Bueno S\'anchez

item.title: Dressed Newton-Cartan geometry and Euclidean thermal configurations in 3D
item.description: arXiv:2611.08471v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We report a new class of solutions of three-dimensional Galilean Anti-de Sitter gravity. The theory can be formulated as a topological gauge theory invariant under the doubly extended Newton-Hooke group in three dimensions. The solution can be interpreted as a dressed Newton-Cartan geometry, which is endowed with four conserved charges: energy, angular momentum, spin and rest mass. Interestingly, the magnitude of the spin turns out to be bounded from above by the rest mass. The Euclidean continuation of the solution exhibits well--defined thermal properties in terms of its gauge theoretical description. Temperature, angular velocity and other chemical potentials are obtained from suitable regularity conditions associated with the topology of a solid torus.
item.dc:creator: Luis Avil\'es, Oscar Fuentealba, Diego Hidalgo, Pablo Rodr\'iguez
